claim_text: Kidney disease can alter vitamin D metabolism and the handling of calcium and phosphate; vitamin D supplementation in chronic kidney disease therefore requires assessment of renal status, biochemical context and existing treatment rather than an automatic dose based on questionnaire answers.
health_goal_or_outcome: Avoid inappropriate vitamin D supplementation in people with kidney disease.

population.age_range: Not specified; requires age- and disease-specific clinical context.
population.other_context: This is a safety-screening statement, not a blanket contraindication.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Vitamin D2 or D3 supplements; active vitamin D analogues are distinct medicines.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Vitamin D Health Professional Fact Sheet summarizes vitamin D metabolism, toxicity and clinical contexts. CKD-specific dosing and monitoring should follow current nephrology guidance.
limitations: CKD stage and biochemical parameters materially affect management.
This claim requires review against current CKD-MBD guidance.
